en: The national flower sampaguita produces highly fragrant white blossoms that typically open at night and close during the daytime.
Our national bird, the Philippine eagle, features a shaggy dark brown crest and hunts primarily in tall dipterocarp forests.
National Scientist Ramon Barba developed a method using potassium nitrate to make mango trees flower and fruit out of season.
The Ifugao people carved the Banaue Rice Terraces into steep mountains, using stone walls to hold irrigation water for growing rice.
The national tree, narra, drops clusters of small yellow flowers during the dry season and yields very hard, red-brown wood.
Marine biologist Angel Alcala built artificial coral reefs to restore fish populations and protect observable marine life in Philippine coastal waters.
The carabao, our national animal, has wide hooves that prevent it from sinking deep into the mud of wet rice paddies.
During the Lucban Pahiyas Festival, residents decorate their house exteriors with colorful kiping, which are vibrant leaf-shaped wafers made from rice paste.
The anahaw palm features large, circular, fan-like leaves that radiate from a single, straight trunk in tropical Philippine forests.
While exiled in Dapitan, Jose Rizal planted numerous fruit trees and built a stone water system to irrigate the local farmlands.
The Mangyan people of Mindoro carve their traditional ambahan poetry onto cured bamboo tubes using a sharp knife to create visible script.
The South Sea pearl, our national gem, forms inside the large Pinctada maxima oyster found in the coral reefs of Palawan.
